Baranow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Baranów, Poland

Not demolished. Baranów's Jewish community, documented from at least 1621 (though likely present earlier), registered 30 Jewish craftsmen by 1626 and grew to a steady 53 percent of the town's population by both 1856 and 1930. This cemetery, likely established around 1600 on a small hill outside town, was destroyed during WWII; tombstones were stolen by residents afterward, and much of the land was converted to arable use or pasture. In recent years, only four matzevot found outside the cemetery, dating from the first half of the 19th century and 1861, have been placed back within its preserved area.
